minutes.headline: Assessors approved two sets of minutes, heard heated lakefront-assessment criticism, and went into executive session on abatements.
minutes.summary: The Board of Assessors approved the December 7 and January 31 minutes (the latter with a correction on who made and seconded a motion). Most of the meeting was public comment from lakefront residents angry about large assessment increases, about who controls the abatement process, and about the legality of the executive session. The board then voted into executive session to discuss abatement and exemption applications, after a resident formally challenged its validity.

public_comment.topic: Public comment limited to about three to four minutes per person.

A resident asked when the board would hold a public meeting on the abatement process, when independent assessors would review, when inspections would begin, and whether applicants could attend hearings.
The same resident asked how the town got into this costly situation, citing a 135 percent lakefront increase while the tax rate fell.
Objected to the board being told not to inspect lakefront properties, and challenged the executive session notice as insufficiently specific under open meeting law.
Asked who is in charge, the board or the select board; criticised the 135 percent lakefront increases against commercial decreases and the late bills, and asked for an outside audit.
Cited the town charter to argue the elected board is independent and should not defer to the town manager or investigation committee; asked for the comparable sales data.
Said only the three assessors can correct a mathematical error through DOR and urged an outside audit.
A resident formally challenged abatements as a valid reason for executive session.

what_happened.line: The Board of Assessors approved two sets of minutes, December 7 and January 31, the second with a correction to who made and seconded a motion.
Lakefront residents spent most of the meeting criticising large assessment increases, late bills and who controls the abatement process.
A resident challenged the executive session notice as too vague under open meeting law, and another formally challenged abatements as a valid reason for one.
The board moved toward executive session on abatement and exemption applications; the vote was not audible in the recording.
Residents with further questions were told to send them in writing, to be copied to the investigation committee.

why_it_matters: Assessments set each property's share of the tax bill, and lakefront owners are disputing how theirs were set and how abatement applications will be handled.
The minutes record no vote on the executive session and no public timetable for the abatement process, so residents cannot yet see how those applications will be decided.
watch_next: A public meeting on the abatement process, which a resident asked the board to schedule; the minutes give no date.
Written resident questions, which are to be copied to the investigation committee.
